answer: Between 3400 and 3000 BCE the relative numbers of monuments and of axes both increased, but each changed differently relative to the three elements of symbolic capital (Hatchets & Swords, Daggers, House Size). All values are Z-standardized proxies (standard-deviation units around each series' own long-term ~4300–500 BCE average; above 0 = above average, below 0 = below average), not raw counts. Monument Count rose modestly from −0.46 to −0.36 (Δ ≈ +0.10, ending near its average) while Axes & Celts rose clearly from +0.37 to +0.80 (Δ ≈ +0.43), both after surging mid-window around 3200 BCE (monuments +0.91, axes +2.60) and then partly retreating — so both rises are real but non-monotonic (Spearman/rank inspection on the five 100-yr bins; no significance claimed, n=5). Relative to the symbolic-capital elements: (1) House Size — the only symbolic element that moved substantially — fell steeply from +2.05 to +0.19 (Δ ≈ −1.86, roughly 4–18× the monument/axe rises in absolute size), i.e. opposed to monuments and axes; the association is inverse (n=5 bins: Pearson ≈ −0.35 for monuments, −0.17 for axes; Spearman ρ ≈ −0.41, −0.37; annual n=401: ≈ −0.40, −0.26 — descriptive only). (2) Hatchets & Swords stayed essentially fixed at ≈ −0.43 (Δ ≈ 0.00) across the whole window, so monument/axe growth was decoupled from this weapon-related symbolic element: the weak correlation is sign-unstable/near zero (monuments: r ≈ +0.28 to +0.29; axes: r ≈ −0.11 on bins vs +0.03 on annual), driven by negligible residual wobble — treat as "no meaningful association," not a positive link. (3) Daggers were completely static at −0.58 with zero variance throughout the window, making their correlation with monuments/axes undefined — a substantive finding in itself: one symbolic element frozen while monuments and axes grew, hence no associated change and no co-movement. Interpretive frame (stated as an assumption): under the study's classification, monuments and axes proxy social and economic capital respectively (not symbolic capital), so the pattern is best described as social- and economic-capital indicators rising (weakly for monuments, strongly for axes, with a mid-window pulse at 3200 BCE) while symbolic capital was internally split — a steep House Size decline, static Hatchets & Swords, and static Daggers. In other words, monument/axe growth decoupled from weapon-related symbolic capital and ran inversely to the House Size symbolic element. For context only (not a symbolic-capital element): pollen-derived landscape openness (Belau+Woserin PC1 MEAN) declined steeply over the same interval, from +0.08 at 3400 BCE to −1.86 at 3000 BCE (≈ −0.63 per century, uniformly negative under every 50–250-year smoothing), coinciding with the monument/axe rise.

payload.hypothesis: 3400-3000 BCE: monument numbers rose weakly (Z −0.46→−0.36, Δ≈+0.10) and axe numbers rose strongly (Z +0.37→+0.80, Δ≈+0.43), both with a mid-window spike at 3200 BCE, while symbolic capital split: House Size fell steeply (Z +2.05→+0.19, Δ≈−1.86) producing an inverse association (r≈−0.2 to −0.4), Hatchets & Swords stayed fixed (~−0.43, decoupled/≈zero r), and Daggers were entirely static (−0.58, zero variance → undefined r). Monuments/axes thus proxy rising social/economic capital decoupled from weapon-symbolic capital and inversely related to the House Size symbolic element.
payload.workflow: Loaded capital.csv (39 native 100-yr bins; German decimals; Z-standardized) and time_series_data.csv (1-yr interpolated series) and verified 37 overlapping bins match to 1e-9; restricted to CE ∈ [−3400,−3000]. Reported per-variable 5-bin values, endpoint ΔZ, Pearson + Spearman correlations of MonumentCount/AxesCelts vs HatchetSword/Dagger/HouseSize at both the 5-bin and annual (n=401) resolution, flagged resolution disagreement for AxesCelts–HatchetSword, treated constant Dagger as undefined-correlation/static finding, and added pollen openness (Belau+Woserin PC1 MEAN) as context. No significance testing; descriptive only.
